title: Hybrid Cache for Amazon S3 Cache Rules
description: Cache rules for Hybrid Cache for Amazon S3, read from cache_rules.json in cache_dir. Each rule matches a glob pattern against the cache key {bucket}/{object_key} and sets any subset of the settings below. Rules resolve per field. For each field, the first matching rule that sets it supplies the value. A field that no matching rule sets takes its global value: from config.yaml, or the built-in default for a field with no global setting. The file is optional. The proxy re-reads it on the first lookup after cache.bucket_settings_staleness_threshold (default: 60s) has passed. While the file is absent or rules is empty, every key uses the global values.

$schema.description: Optional reference to this schema, for validation in an editor.

rules.description: Ordered list of at most 1024 rules; a file with more fails validation. Order matters: for each field the first matching rule that sets it wins, so put specific rules above broad ones. An empty list leaves every key on the global values.

cache_rule.description: One rule: a required glob pattern and any subset of the settings below.

pattern.description: Glob pattern matched against the whole cache key {bucket}/{object_key}, with no leading slash. '*' matches any run of characters except '/', '**' matches any run including '/', and '?' matches one character except '/'. Every other character matches itself, so '.' matches only a dot. Matching is case-sensitive and must cover the whole key. A leading bucket name ("mybucket/temp/**") limits a rule to one bucket, a leading '**' ("**/logs/**") matches in every bucket, and '**' before a literal segment ("**/credit-cards/**") matches that segment at any depth. Must be non-empty. Keys for access points, Multi-Region Access Points and S3-compatible hosts start with a different first segment ({name}-{account}-s3alias, {alias}.mrap, or the bare normalized path); see docs/CACHING.md.

get_ttl.description: How long a cached GET response is served without contacting S3. A duration such as "0s", "30s", "5m", "1h" or "7d"; a number without a unit is seconds (see docs/CONFIGURATION.md, Duration format). "0s" keeps the object on disk but revalidates it with S3 on every request, and keeps its ranges out of the RAM cache (ram_cache_eligible is forced false).

head_ttl.description: How long a cached HEAD response is served without contacting S3. Same format as get_ttl. "0s" revalidates every HEAD with S3.

put_ttl.description: How long an object in the write cache stays cached before its first GET, which moves it to get_ttl. Same format as get_ttl.

read_cache_enabled.description: Whether GET responses for matching keys are cached. false streams them from S3 without caching them on disk or in RAM, and forces ram_cache_eligible to false. The write cache is set separately. Default: the global cache.read_cache_enabled (true).

write_cache_enabled.description: Whether PUT requests to matching keys are cached in the write cache. false forwards them to S3 without caching them. Default: the global cache.write_cache_enabled (true).

compression_enabled.description: Whether cached data for matching keys is LZ4-compressed. This overrides the built-in extension denylist in either direction: true compresses a denylisted extension, and false skips a compressible one. The denylist covers formats that are already compressed, such as images, video, archives, documents and executables; docs/COMPRESSION.md has the full list. Default: the global compression.enabled.

ram_cache_eligible.description: Whether range data for matching keys may be stored in the RAM cache. false keeps the RAM cache for other keys. Forced to false when get_ttl is "0s" or read_cache_enabled is false. Default: true.

evaluate_conditions_from_cache.description: Whether a GET, range GET or HEAD whose only conditional header is If-Match or If-Range is answered from the cache. With true, an unexpired entry under a non-zero get_ttl whose ETag matches is served without contacting S3; an If-Range validator must strong-match the cached ETag, and a HEAD also needs its cached HEAD entry within head_ttl. Any other conditional header, a mix of conditional headers, a mismatch or a miss is forwarded to S3. With false, every conditional request is forwarded, so S3 decides every precondition. Default: the global cache.evaluate_conditions_from_cache (true).

page_widening.description: Turns on page-aligned range caching for matching keys. An eligible small range GET (shorter than page_size, with an unsigned Range header and no partNumber) is widened to a fixed-size, page-aligned fetch, and the whole page is cached on disk and in RAM. It is off by default, and only a rule can turn it on, because widening fetches more bytes than the client asked for. Widening helps when reads fall within one page, such as Parquet or ORC footer and column-chunk reads, and adds transfer when reads are scattered. See docs/CACHE_READ_PATHS.md, Page-aligned range caching. Default: false.

page_size.description: Page size in bytes for page-aligned range caching; applies only where page_widening is true. Pages sit on a fixed grid that starts at offset 0. Must be greater than 0 and at most 67108864 (64 MiB, the RAM cache's admission ceiling); a rule that turns on page_widening with a page_size outside that range fails validation. Default: 16777216 (16 MiB).

hedging_enabled.description: Turns on hedged upstream requests for matching keys. When the first S3 fetch has not returned its first byte within hedge_trigger_after, the proxy sends a second identical fetch and serves whichever responds first. It is off by default, and only a rule can turn it on, because each hedge is a duplicate S3 request and the right trigger depends on the workload. See docs/HEDGING.md for the cost governor and when hedging helps. Default: false.

hedge_trigger_after.description: Time to first byte after which a hedge is sent; applies only where hedging_enabled is true. Must be greater than 0 and less than connection_pool.upstream_first_byte_timeout (default: 5s); checked each time the rules load. Same format as get_ttl. Default: "250ms".

hedge_max_per_request.description: Most hedges per client request. A range GET that fans out into several missing-range fetches shares one budget across all of them. Default: 1.
